newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt should say sorry to Aborigines-poll.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt should say sorry to Aborigines-poll.

text.p: About 50 percent of Australians believe the government should apologise to Aborigines for the forced removal of children from their families, according to a newspaper opinion poll published on Tuesday.
The Australian newspaper's Newspoll found 40 percent of Australians believed no apology was needed, while 10 percent were uncommitted.

Prime Minister John Howard has ruled out a formal national apology in response to the "stolen generations" report released last week, saying Australians could not be held legally responsible for the sins of the past.
But the poll also found an increase in support for both the government and the prime minister over the past two weeks, despite the lack of an apology.
Primary vote support for the conservative Liberal-National coalition rose two percentage points to 43 percent over that period, the poll found.
"The latest Newspoll shows the satisfaction rating of the prime minister is recovering from its lowest level since the election last year," the newspaper said.
The poll found 42 percent of the voters surveyed were satisfied with Howard's performance, up from 37 percent two weeks ago.
Primary vote support for the Labor opposition was unchanged at 37 percent, while opposition leader Kim Beazley's satisfaction rating dropped to 38 percent from 44 percent.

The latest result compares with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 1996 election, which swept the Coalition into power and ended 13 years of Labor rule.
The poll also showed primary vote support for race row politician Pauline Hanson's One Nation party dropped two percentage points to seven percent.
The poll surveyed 1,146 voters around the country by telephone last weekend.
